Definition: from a compound of G4862 and G2239; mutual habituation, i.e. usage:--custom.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says if any man seems contentious, we have no such custom, neither the churches of God, and Pilate reminds the Jews that they have a custom that he should release one prisoner at the passover. Custom can settle a church dispute or free a prisoner, and in both cases the question is whether the custom serves the truth or only the habit.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that custom must serve the truth, and I believe no habit of the churches is worth keeping if it contradicts the gospel.
